title: The Healthcare Election: Florida
description: When federal subsidies for Affordable Care Act health insurance expired last year, Florida was hit particularly hard. Now, as the election and open enrollment coincide, healthcare is a major issue.

title: Politics, norms and the DOJ's unprecedented pre-election headlines
description: The Justice Department, contrary to past norms, has stayed in the headlines in the run-up to the midterm election.

title: Week in Politics: Trump's Midwest pivot; sharper Democratic messaging
description: The president heads to the midwest for two rallies he previously said were cancelled. Has his message changed this campaign season and how have Democrats sharpened their messaging?

title: Can I trust the polls? And other questions from listeners about the 2026 midterms
description: Ahead of Election Day, listeners send in questions about whether debates are dead, if polls are reliable for election coverage and how Trump might work with Democrats if they win control of Congress.

title: Judge orders an inquiry into potential DOJ misconduct in Trump's golf course case
description: A federal judge is opening an formal inquiry into Trump officials' conduct in the East Potomac case, including whether they misled the court about their plans for the municipal golf course.

title: NPR special: 5 takeaways from a year of listening to swing voters
description: Every election, there is a crucial sliver of voters who help determine which candidates win. Here are five takeaways from a year of listening to voters who backed Biden in 2020 and then Trump in 2024.

title: Why is the Cheesecake Factory at the center of the latest culture war?
description: A joke by former President Obama has gone viral and received backlash from the Trump administration as the issue of affordability looms large over next week's midterm elections.

title: Alaska's Senate race faces claims of spoiler candidate. And, Hegseth ousts Army general
description: Alaska's governor ordered an investigation into claims that Dems recruited a spoiler candidate to confuse voters. And, Hegseth ousted an Army general as the U.S. prepares for potential attacks on Iran.

title: Websites pretending to be local news are boosting Democratic candidates
description: The websites of unknown origin are targeting key U.S. House races. They are getting picked up by ChatGPT's responses but Google's products avoid promoting them.

title: 'Affordability? For who?' Voters decide between helping homeowners or public services
description: Candidates across the U.S. have paid lip service to affordability issues. In Florida, the question of how to save voters money, and at what cost, is literally on the ballot.
